claim: In the same model at Peclet number 10, the glass-transition volume fraction rises steeply and nonlinearly with the active fraction: 5% active particles already move the transition far from the passive case, while going from 35% to 50% moves it little; the crossover fits phi_G(alpha) = phi_0 + a1*alpha^b1 with a1 about 0.064 and b1 about 0.16, phi_0 = 0.61 being the passive value the authors take from earlier work.

numbers.name: active_fraction
numbers.note: the smallest active fraction shown to shift the transition strongly.

numbers.name: peclet_number_steric
numbers.note: Peclet number of the volume-fraction scan.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Dry three-dimensional mixture of soft repulsive spheres (a harmonic repulsion approximated by a Morse form), half small and half large (radius ratio sqrt(2)) in both the active and the passive population; active particles are overdamped active Brownian particles, passive ones have no propulsion; kT = 1e-4, Dr = 3 Dt/a0^2 with a0 the small diameter; steady shear with Lees-Edwards boundaries; Euler-Maruyama at time step 1e-2 in HOOMD-blue (version not stated); total strain 10 with the first 5 discarded; no hydrodynamics, no walls, no friction. Peclet number v0/(a0 Dr), which is peclet_number_steric with the small diameter as the length. Shear rates in model units from 1e-6 to 1e-2. Volume fractions (three dimensions) from 0.60 to 0.72. Volume fractions 0.60 to 0.72 and active fractions 0 to 0.5 at Peclet number 10. The exponent b1 well below one is the paper's evidence that the glass density depends strongly and nonlinearly on the active fraction. phi_0 = 0.61 is cited (Ikeda, Berthier and Sollich 2012; Wiese, Kroy and Levis 2023), not found here, and is not asserted by this entry.
